-Sand mining ear Badonkalan is taking place in huge amounts. This location is close to Goraghat-Dabra highway

- Most tractors did not give us lift

- On the way, at one place, the tractor stopped, and the driver went to a cabin / house like structure and came back

On this route only the people involved in sand and morram mining were seen.

- Datia DSR 2022 mentions 3 mining sites in BadonKalan (BadonKalan - D, A, E - of areas 23, 23, 24.094 Ha respectively)

- Comparing Datia DSR 2022 and other DSRs of districts from which River Sindh flows, we found that BadonKalan is the biggest mining site on River Sindh.

column1: Bardhamann Upriver Sites, Damodar River - 9th March 2024
column6: JCB, jet suction machines, some attached to boats. We interviewed freelance laborers who own and operate their own motorboats. They dig up sand using large perforated buckets (usually from the opposive bank, where there is no mechanised presence), load up their boats with it and deliver it to the main mining site. It is possible that mine operators are using this tactic to get around concession regulations using this for-hire low impact approach
column7:
Sprawling site just upriver from Bardhamann city. Spoke to 2 sand miners (freelance)

Been working at this site for more than 15 years. Pay is about 1000-2000 per day for working till 3pm. They manually dig sand from flooded areas with perforated buckets; they load those onto small mechanized boats that then take it to the other side and deposit it for the excavators, who then presumably load it onto trucks. We observed about 50 trucks at this large site. We observed quite a few motorized boats with cargo of sand plying the river.

These two miners have been working this site for about 15 years, and consider it a very profitable enterprise.


We observed boats with suction heads attached by pipes to some central vacuum and cleaner that deposits the sand in piles. These are the ones that likely cause the perfectly round or oval depressions we see


Second interviewee (a local not involved with mining) said mining doesn't stop in the monsoon.

District is actually Purba Bardhamann

column1: Akalwara, Madhya Pradesh - Narmada River, 10th March 2024
column7:
I noticed many tractor marks - two kinds of marks mostly - one of a tractor and another was, I think, a machine that is used to extract sand, maybe a small dredger. I was travelling with the Narmada Bachao Aandolan (NBA) activists in their van. They told me that people recognise them, especially the people involved with the Sand Mafia and they immediately call and inform those on the sites to pack and leave or hide their machines and equipment. As soon as we reached the Akalwara sand mining site in Barwani district in Madhya Pradesh, we noticed a tractor scrambling away from the site and people running away with it. 

I could see mounds and heaps of sand next to deep dug pits. It looked artificially dug up and evidently not a result of wind and water erosion near the banks. The tractor marks, the pattern of pits and mounds alternatively and the tractor driving away rapidly were signs that illegal sand mining definitely takes place here

column1: Mandawar Village - Shamli District, Uttar Pradesh, Yamuna River - 22nd March 2024
column6: 5 excavators. Multiple trucks and tractors trollies.
column7:
5 excavators were mining sand directly from within the river. And multiple trucks and tractors trollies were running all over the floodplains carrying this sand away from the river.


Our assessment based on official documents says that:


1. There has not been any auction for the sand here.

2. There is no District Survey Report that forms the basis of any auctions


Locally sourced information says that about 200 trucks are taking sand away from this location per day, each selling at a base price of ₹5000.


At 8 months of operation in a year (or till the time that the sand runs out), that comes out to be ₹10,00,000 per day or ₹3,00,00,000 per month or ₹24,00,00,000 over a period of 8 months. This is lost public revenue.


The map above is showing from a day when there was cloud cover, so I've included a satellite image of the location from 20th December 2023 and 19th March 2024 to show you the location and give you a sense of what's going on. See how the sand bank vanishes.


Imagery source: Sentinel-2 L2A.

column1: Yamuna river, Sector-125/126, NOIDA, Gautam Buddh Nagar, UP- 07.12.2021
column7:
The site was being mined for sand. I could remember seeing at least two poclain machines extracting the sand from the middle of the river channel which is basically against the guidelines of Uttar Pradesh Minor Minerals (Concession) Rules, 2021. Artificial sand bars had been created to direct the river flow. Scores and scores of trucks laden with sand could be seen every day. There's an entire makeshift settlement for the laborers who are being employed to mine sand. The location is about a kilometer downstream from Okhla Bird Sanctuary. 

The people at the site asked us not to take any pictures and leave the site. We were also questioned about where are you from, are you a journalist, what have you come here for, etc.?

column1: Ken river - Banda, Uttar Pradesh - 21st Feb 2026
column7: अर्थ मूविंग प्रतिबंधित मशीनों से अवैध खनन

Active mining right near the bridge pillar. Backhoe digging sand, also men with shovels. Loading sand into tractors which are taking the sand up some kaccha rastas. Deep cuts in the bank, lines with piles of sand. Loud tractor sounds, horns and music. Two years ago, there were only signs of mining, but had seen many gharial and muggers on the same bank. Entire area to the side of the mine (adjoining a second mining site, also shows a lot of scraping and scarring). Three muggers at the edge.

Just under the highway bridge, very close to the bridge. Lots of machines, heavy scale of mining.

Atleast 8-10 tractors collecting sand at one time and many others continuously taking turns.

Atleast 100 or more machines mining and transporting sand. Edges of the sand bank have vanished. Mining is close to the highway bridge. Lots of sand piled farther from the bank (where officials "mixed" mud to ruin the mining. But this is unsuccessful effort, since the mining is going on at full scale.)

Active mining close to the bridge pillar. Poclains digging up sand from pits filled with water. Large heaps of sand, sand being piled into tractors and transported up via kaccha rasta. Loud music, machinery sounds. Some waterbirds and two crocodiles basking at the edge. Two years ago this site was an intact bank with some cauliflower mining scars, with multiple muggers, turtles, gharial, and waterbirds - including skimmers. Little further down had spotted a fox

bakaspure village,karra block ,karo bank

This location was within a forest area. This is not a demarcated location for sand mining. This means it is illegal mining. There was sand deposits also in this location.

80+ trucks carrying sand, sand being extracted actively using poclains. Bundh created to enable instream mining, giving access to center of stream and affecting river flow. Close to the Ken river bridge.
